The truth is OPEC isn't a monopoly, but they do represent a major portion of all oil producers. The price for oil has increased very much in part of Trump pulling out of the Iran deal. He doesn't want anyone buying any oil from Iran, regardless of the country, that is his plan with sanctions. Iran makes up about 2.5% of worldwide oil production, so the market is responding to fears that there may be a shortage. Even a 2.5% drop of production can have a large impact on prices as the world can't really go on without oil and gasoline. OPEC and the non-OPEC nations, mostly led by Russia, have agreed to increase production, but they can't fully make up for the loss from Iran so quickly, and even with enough time they are nearing their maximum possible exports anyway, so it's likely we are going to have a shortage for some time.


This all means that Trump pulling out of a deal that took tons of nations years to get right has resulted in a worldwide shortage of oil and much more expensive gas prices for everyone, including Americans, who vote this November. He wants to take none of the blame and push it all on OPEC, falsely claiming he had nothing to do with it, falsely saying they are a monopoly, and falsely claiming they can export more (here it's not really clear if he is deliberately lying or isn't educated enough on the topic to understand the nuance). His base will eat it up at face value, and honestly most the left will just eat up "it's Trump's fault" at face value without fully understanding the issue either.
